headline: Re-reading 2009-2026 EU tax-benefit rules through optimal-transfer theory: the paper's "in-work transfer beats demogrant" result survives and is strengthened post-2017 (critical elasticity fell 0.22->0.13), but it is explicitly elasticity-contingent - it holds for 0/14 countries at a US-EITC-style zero participation response and 9/14 at Chetty-sized elasticities in 2026.

figures.caption: Elasticity frontier by era in (avg extensive elasticity eta-bar, intensive elasticity eps) space. Blue = Psi_w<Psi_d boundary (in-work cheaper to the right), green = Psi_w<1, orange = Pareto; curves are the median over the fixed panel {FI,FR,EL,IT,SE}. Vertical bands = post-2007 extensive-elasticity evidence, labelled by origin (Kleven is US EITC; Chetty mostly US). The in-work-cheaper boundary moved left (easier) after 2015.

notes: Study B of the welfare-reform follow-up: CPU-only, no EUROMOD runs, no fetches. Seeded from followup/002-living-update-cont (the completed continuation of 001-living-update); reuses its rates and the replication's welfare_core/formula layer unchanged.

Respects Study A: validated set V = 14 countries, headline regime V4 (q=0, 7 UB-leg fallbacks), no 'tau unvalidated' country (gate-3c medians <=0.55pp). Inherits its Psi-instability for the lower deciles.

Inverse-optimum item is a [CONSISTENCY CHECK], not a test; the strict g<0 iff over-predicts Pareto in 2026 for AT/NL/ES (participation-trap, Psi-unstable), flagged not hidden. The minimal amendment (eta on secondary earners/lone parents) barely moves the 2026 ranking - the level of bottom-decile PTRs, not composition, is the driver.

The word 'validation' is used only for the Belgium external check (item 4b); the model cost per job sits below the published de Mahieu (2021) range, the pre-declared expected direction. Belgium is the only study country with a cited cost-per-job estimate.

1998 values are survey-cell averages and 2026 values are hypothetical households (method break) - never joined. Claims tagged [ESTIMATED]/[CALIBRATED]/[CONSISTENCY CHECK]/[PROPOSED] in theory_update.md.
